function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph).
• In cities: 25–35 mph.
• Rural roads: 55 mph unless posted otherwise. | Speed limits can be lower in construction zones or school zones. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑seat or booster.
• Children under 4 must be in a rear‑seat child‑seat. | Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Violations carry a $50 fine plus points on the driver’s record. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, possible jail time. | Texas has a “zero‑tolerance” law for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02 %). | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has the right of way.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | Failure to yield can lead to traffic citations. | | **School‑Zone Speed Limits** | • 20 mph in school zones during school hours.
• 25 mph in school zones outside school hours. | Speeding in school zones can result in higher fines and points. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Passing on the right is prohibited unless the left lane is occupied. | Improper lane changes can lead to citations. | | **Headlights & Lighting** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise, or when visibility is reduced.
• Fog lights are allowed only in fog or heavy rain. | Failure to use headlights can result in a fine. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a crosswalk or intersection.
• No parking in fire lanes or on sidewalks. | Violations can lead to towing and fines. | | **Traffic Signal Violations** | • Red‑light running, stop‑sign violations, and failure to yield at a green light are punishable. | Points added to the driver’s record; fines vary by county. | | **Points System** | • 3 points for a first offense, 4 for a second, 5 for a third.
• 12 points in 12 months leads to license suspension. | Points can be reduced through a defensive‑driving course. | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for total bodily injury, $25,000 for property damage. | Failure to maintain insurance can result in license suspension. | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Trucks over 10,000 lb must have a commercial driver’s license (CDL).
• Bicycles must obey the same traffic laws as motor vehicles. | Commercial vehicles must display proper placards. | | **Roadside Assistance & Emergencies** | • Call 911 for emergencies.
• For non‑emergencies, use the Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) roadside assistance. | No fines for calling for help. | ### How to Find More Detailed Information 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The official legal text is available online at the Texas Legislature’s website. 2. **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** – Offers guides, brochures, and FAQs on driving laws. 3. **Local County Courts** – For specific citation details and penalties. 4. **Legal Aid Organizations** – Provide assistance if you receive a traffic ticket or DUI charge. --- **Quick Tips for Texas Drivers** - **Always obey posted speed limits** – they’re the law. - **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk on the phone. - **Check your mirrors** before changing lanes. - **Keep your insurance up to date** to avoid license suspension. - **Be extra cautious in school zones** – speed limits are lower and enforcement is strict. If you need more specific information (e.g., how to contest a ticket, details on a particular county’s enforcement practices, or the latest updates to the Texas Transportation Code), let me know!
